subject: Request: Temporary SLA routing + latency guardrail for Rooster-2B preview launch
body:
From: Sam Walters <sam.walters@brightedge.ai>
To: alex_martinez@redwood.ai
Cc: Christine Park <c.park@brightedge.ai>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: Temporary SLA routing + latency guardrail for Rooster-2B preview launch

Hi Alex,

Quick context: we're moving Rooster-2B-preview into a limited production rollout next week for a small set of users. The model performs well in evals, but we've seen occasional tail latency spikes during warmups. Our security/compliance team also requires deterministic routing (dedicated pools) for the initial release.

Can Redwood provide a temporary SLA carve-out that routes traffic for the /v1/generate-rooster endpoint to a dedicated pool with a 90ms p50 target and a relaxed p99 (600ms) for the first 14 days? We'd like this in writing so we can align with our procurement/legal folks. If dedicated capacity isn't feasible, would a guaranteed regional routing + automatic fallback to hosted nodes with explicit traffic shaping work?

Attached is a one-page rollout plan. We're on a tight timeline and would appreciate a decision by EOD Wednesday.

Thanks,
Sam
Sam Walters
Head of Product
BrightEdge AI

---

On Mon, 16 Nov 2026 at 10:03, Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.ai> wrote:
To: Sam Walters <sam.walters@brightedge.ai>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Subject: RE: Request: Temporary SLA routing + latency guardrail for Rooster-2B preview launch

Sam — thanks for the clear ask and the plan. Looping in Laura (Product) and Karthik (Infra) to assess feasibility and constraints.

Short answer: we can consider a limited temporary exception but need to lock in monitoring, rollback triggers, and a capacity/commitment agreement from BrightEdge. Laura/Karthik — any immediate red flags?

Alex Martinez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

---

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: alex_martinez@redwood.ai, Sam Walters <sam.walters@brightedge.ai>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 11:20:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Request: Temporary SLA routing + latency guardrail for Rooster-2B preview launch

Thanks, Alex. Sam — appreciate the details. A few technical/operational notes: 

- Dedicated pool: we can reserve a small dedicated pool for the endpoint for a 14-day window, but it requires a minimum committed throughput (we'll need the expected RPS and concurrent sessions). Without that commit, capacity could be preempted.
- Latency targets: we can accept p50=90ms and p99 up to 600ms for the preview window, but it will be logged as a temporary SLA exception tied to the dedicated pool. Production SLAs will apply after the window.
- Fallback behavior: we recommend a deterministic fallback policy — if dedicated pool p99 exceeds 1s for >5 minutes, auto-redirect traffic to a regional hosted pool with concurrency limiting and degrade responses gracefully.
- Monitoring & rollback: we need exportable dashboards and two bistream alerts (ops + your on-call) before enabling. We'll also require a signed SLA exception form and an internal runbook for rollbacks.

I've attached a draft SLA exception form and a quick screenshot from our latency dashboard showing similar past previews. If you can provide the expected traffic profile by EOD tomorrow, we can generate an exception package for legal sign-off.

Attachments: sla_exception_form.pdf (PDF), latency-dashboard.png (PNG)

Laura Bennett
Product Lead, Runtime
Redwood Inference

---

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, alex_martinez@redwood.ai, Sam Walters <sam.walters@brightedge.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Request: Temporary SLA routing + latency guardrail for Rooster-2B preview launch

Looping infra in (raising to ops): technically doable with caveats. Operational checklist we need completed before enabling: 

1) Traffic profile (RPS/peak concurrent sessions)
2) Canary schedule and traffic ramp plan (5%, 25%, 50%, 100% over 48h windows)
3) Alerting endpoints (PagerDuty + SN for your ops team)
4) Acceptable cost offset (dedicated pool pricing difference) — procurement needs to sign off

If those are provided, infra can pre-provision a 2-GPU dedicated pool and the routing rules. We will enable the deterministic fallback and the automatic rollback trigger described by Laura.

Karthik Iyer
Director, Infrastructure
Redwood Inference

---

From: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Walters <sam.walters@brightedge.ai>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 17:03:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Request: Temporary SLA routing + latency guardrail for Rooster-2B preview launch

Sam —

We've reviewed and can approve a 14-day temporary SLA exception tied to a pre-provisioned dedicated pool for /v1/generate-rooster with the following binding conditions: 

- Contracted minimum throughput: 120 RPS sustained (you indicated ~90 RPS peak; please confirm).
- SLOs for the window: p50 <= 90ms, p99 <= 600ms. If p99 > 1s for more than 5 minutes, traffic will be auto-rerouted per the fallback policy.
- Monitoring: Redwood will provide dashboard access and set up two alert hooks (ops + your on-call).
- Cost: BrightEdge to accept the dedicated pool surcharge for the 14-day period; procurement will sign the SLA exception form via DocuSign.
- Rollout plan: follow the canary ramp 5/25/50/100% over 48h. Infra must be notified 24h before each ramp step.

Next steps for you: 1) confirm RPS/concurrency, 2) sign the SLA exception form (I've uploaded the draft to HubSpot and attached the PDF), 3) provide PagerDuty endpoint for alerts. We'll provision upon receipt.

HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/8421
Exception doc: https://redwood-internal/docs/slo-exceptions/DEAL-8421

Happy to have Karthik and Laura jump in on operational calls tomorrow if helpful.

Best,
Alex Martinez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
